reference.title: Useful expressions for explaining a word that you don’t know
rows: It’s somebody who shows you round a city or a museum. (a guide)
It’s something which we use to pay, instead of cash. (a credit card)
It’s somewhere where people go when they want to send a parcel or a letter. (a post office)
It’s a kind of fruit. It’s long and yellow. (a banana)
It’s like a sweater, but it has buttons. (a cardigan)
It’s similar to a wallet, but it’s for a woman. (a purse)
It’s a verb. For example, you do this to the TV when you’ve finished watching something. (turn off)

reference.title: Paraphrasing
reference.text: If you don’t know a word in English, don’t stop: explain it with other words you know. Say what kind of thing it is (a person, a thing, a place, a verb, an adjective), then give a detail or an example.

reference.wrong: It’s somewhere which you can buy bread.
reference.right: It’s somewhere where you can buy bread.

reference.title: Silent e
reference.text: e at the end of a word is normally not pronounced, but it usually changes the sound of the vowel before it. When a word ends in silent e, the preceding vowel sound is usually the same as that letter of the alphabet, e.g. sit /sɪt/, site /saɪt/, fat /fæt/, fate /feɪt/.

reference.title: A to Z
reference.text: In this game there is a wheel with 25 letters of the alphabet (not including ‘X’). The presenter gives definitions for words starting with the letters, e.g. ‘A – the place where you catch a plane’ = ‘Airport’. If the contestant can’t think of the word, he or she says ‘Pass’.

tasks.instruction: Read about the game show A to Z and answer the questions
tasks.note: SB 1b–c; текст — в context, картинка из SB p.26 (tools/images.py); ответы — по тексту (MODEL). 1a (составить слова из букв на странице) не перенесено
tasks.context:
In this game there is a wheel with 25 letters of the alphabet (not including ‘X’). The aim of the game is to complete the alphabet wheel by saying the correct word for each letter in five minutes. The presenter gives the contestant definitions for words starting with the letters, for example, ‘A – the place where you catch a plane’ = ‘Airport’.

To start the game the presenter reads a definition for a word which begins with A and the contestant has to quickly say the word. If the contestant can’t think of the word, he or she says ‘Pass’. When a contestant passes or gets a word wrong, the presenter goes on to the next letter.

The presenter continues round the wheel to Z, then starts from the beginning again. The presenter repeats the definitions that the contestant passed on or got wrong, until five minutes is up. If a contestant gets all 25 words right, he or she wins the prize.

reference.title: who, which, where
rows: That’s the woman who won the lottery last year. A chef is a person who cooks food in a restaurant.
A clock is something which tells the time. Is that the book which won an important prize?
A post office is a place where you can buy stamps. That’s the restaurant where I had dinner last week.

reference.title: Defining relative clauses
reference.text: We use defining relative clauses to explain what a person, thing or place is or does. The verb after where needs a subject, e.g. you: a place where you can buy stamps. We can also use which to talk about a place: A post office is a place which sells stamps.

reference.title: that
reference.text: We can use that instead of who or which: She’s the girl who / that works with my brother. It’s a thing which / that connects two computers. Don’t use that instead of where.

reference.wrong: A chef is a person which cooks food.
reference.right: A chef is a person who cooks food.
reference.why: who for people, which for things.

reference.wrong: That’s the restaurant where I had dinner there.
reference.right: That’s the restaurant where I had dinner.
reference.why: Don’t repeat the place (there) after where.

reference.wrong: A post office is a place where sells stamps.
reference.right: A post office is a place which sells stamps. / A post office is a place where you can buy stamps.
reference.why: After where you need a subject + verb.

tasks.instruction: Role-play: you are a customer in a restaurant. Order a meal and complain about a problem
tasks.note: SB PE2 3d–e (A — customer)

exercises.situation: You are a waiter in a restaurant in New York. The student is a customer (level: pre-intermediate). Use the phrases from the episode: Are you ready to order? Can I get you something to start with? How would you like your steak? Would you like that with fries or a baked potato? And to drink? Still or sparkling? Menu: starters — tomato soup, garlic mushrooms; main courses — steak, grilled tuna, chicken with rice, vegetable pasta; desserts — chocolate cake, ice cream. Take the order one question at a time. Then bring the food, but make one mistake (bring the wrong side dish, or cook the steak wrong). Wait for the student to complain politely and offer to do something with I’ll… (I’ll change it. / I’ll take it back to the kitchen.). Call the student sir or madam.
exercises.goal: Order a meal in a restaurant and complain politely about a problem.
exercises.opener: Good evening. Here’s the menu. Are you ready to order?
criteria: orders a main course and a drink, and answers about the starter
uses I’d like… / I’ll have…
answers the waiter’s questions (how the steak is cooked, still or sparkling)
complains politely: I’m sorry, but I asked for…

steps.example: I’d like the chicken with rice, please.
I’m sorry, but I asked for a baked potato, not fries.

tasks.instruction: Swap roles: you are the waiter. Take the customer’s order and deal with the problem
tasks.note: SB PE2 3e (B — waiter)

exercises.situation: You are a customer in a restaurant in New York; the student is the waiter (level: pre-intermediate). Menu: starters — tomato soup, garlic mushrooms; main courses — steak, grilled tuna, chicken with rice, vegetable pasta; desserts — chocolate cake, ice cream. Answer the waiter’s questions one at a time: no starter, the steak medium with a baked potato, still water. When the waiter says the food is here, complain: I’m sorry, but I asked for my steak medium, and this is well done. Wait for the waiter to apologize and offer to do something. At the end ask for the bill. If the student forgets a question (how you want your steak, what to drink), prompt them naturally.
exercises.goal: You are the waiter: take the order, bring the food and deal with the complaint.
exercises.opener: Excuse me! I’d like to order, please.
criteria: asks Are you ready to order? and the follow-up questions
asks how the customer would like the steak and what to drink
apologizes and offers to do something with I’ll…
uses sir or madam

steps.example: How would you like your steak? Rare, medium, or well done?
I’m really sorry, madam. I’ll take it back to the kitchen.
